answer: Credit both, but for different acts, and keep the clerk's role marked as the cataloguer's inference rather than fact. Separate the intellectual composition of the text from the physical act of signing: model an E65 Creation event whose P94 has created points to the letter's content as an E33 Linguistic Object, and whose P14 carried out by points to the actor(s) involved, qualified with P14.1 in the role of (e.g. 'drafter' vs 'signatory') so the secretary's and clerk's contributions are not collapsed into one undifferentiated 'author'. The physical letter is an E22 Human-Made Object that P128 carries the E33 text and P65 shows visual item the secretary's signature as an E37 Mark -- keeping the signature itself (well-evidenced, physically present) modeled separately from composition of the wording (the part actually in dispute). Because the clerk's authorship is the cataloguer's own comparative judgement (handwriting/letterhead), not a fact recorded anywhere in the collection, wrap that specific P14 claim in an E13 Attribute Assignment: the cataloguer's assessment activity P140 assigned attribute to the Creation event, P141 assigned the (unnamed) clerk as an E21 Person, P177 assigned property of type P14, with P3 has note carrying the evidentiary basis. This is exactly what E13's scope note is for: registering someone's opinion about a property without asserting it as the knowledge base's own settled claim, and it lets the secretary's signing stand on firmer, undisputed footing while the clerk's drafting stays visibly provisional. Note honestly that CRM has no agreed formal confidence/uncertainty calculus beyond this reification pattern -- the SIG's own attempt to add a generic '.2' certainty property (Issue 349, still Open) was explicitly not adopted, and Martin Doerr himself flagged E13 as 'computationally heavy' for this purpose in the same discussion, so this is the best available mechanism, not a fully satisfying one.

rejected_alternatives.option: Flat P14 carried out by pointing only at the secretary (the catalogued attribution)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Would assert as settled fact exactly the claim the cataloguer doubts; contradicts the cataloguer's own comparative evidence and the case's explicit uncertainty.

rejected_alternatives.option: Modeling the signing itself as the E65 Creation of the letter's content (secretary as sole P94 has created participant)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Signing does not produce new conceptual/linguistic content -- concept E65's scope note is about creation of conceptual items, not authorization of an existing text. Conflating it with authorship misattributes the wording. Kept the signature instead as an E37 Mark shown on the physical carrier (P65), separate from the E33 Linguistic Object's creation.

rejected_alternatives.option: CRMinf I2 Belief / argumentation apparatus for the uncertainty
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Surfaced via P94's incoming properties (J27/J7) and Issue 349's thread, but this is heavier machinery for building explicit scholarly argument chains from evidence; a single cataloguing judgement is adequately (if imperfectly) captured by E13 Attribute Assignment, which is the mechanism the reference model itself names for 'someone's opinion' about a property.
